parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a hostile national layer plus a protective state layer. National exposures are traveller-facing and documented: entry officers told to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; an executive order excluding trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (tier-1 universal exposure, remedy undocumented); corrections-bureau conversion-therapy-style policies and documented abuse in immigration custody. The division adds its own minor-care and sports bans. Countervailing and operative: public-accommodations and employment protections since 2018/2020 with documented 2026 enforcement, hate-crime enhancements, abolished panic defence, 88% public support, and a state court protecting trans students. No documented arrest or facility ban in this division; incident census lacks a denominator.

entry_documents.exposure: February 2025 order ended X markers; officers instructed to refuse where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex and to consider fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; reports of passports blocked/confiscated stranding travellers; foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Challenges pending in national courts; existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud finding can precede any state-level protection; state equality law cannot displace federal adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal); transgender immigration detainees reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse by guards; prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; ongoing litigation noted; state abolished gay/trans panic defence (2024).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally (visa, fraud allegation) enters these custody practices before state remedies apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities — tier-1 universal exposure; nationally 9+1 units ban identity-congruent facility use in all government buildings, 4 units criminalise in certain circumstances; division's own ban status not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations (2018, extended 2020); state court protected trans students in August 2024.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State accommodations law does not cancel the federal facility order in federally owned or funded buildings.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors (2024, expanded 2026) with disciplinary and private-right-of-action provisions — direct exposure for a traveller with a trans minor; national orders and proposed rules target youth care and subpoenaed hospital records.
care_services.protection: Grandfather clause for care underway; division lifted public-insurance surgery exclusion (2017); adult care not banned by the division.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces the state ban plus federal hostility; a minor needing emergency care interacts with the federal facility rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice department 'radical gender ideology' framing; orders directing investigation of schools promoting 'gender ideology'; 66% national poll support for birth-sex-only documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division poll: 88% support for SOGI discrimination protections (2022); no state threat-framing documented; federal orders partly enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal rhetoric raises outing and enforcement probability; division public opinion mitigates street-level but not federal encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans youth care and trans girls' sports (birth certificate required for eligibility); federal order criminalising teachers facilitating social transition signals climate; parent opt-out from gender-identity instruction.
minors_guardians.protection: State high court 3-1 protected transgender students (Aug 2024); anti-bullying law covers gender identity/expression; conversion-therapy ban survived repeal attempt.
minors_guardians.interaction: School and sports rules reach a visiting minor only in schools/sport settings; care ban reaches any medical encounter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025, second-highest raw count — no denominator, so rate unestablished; national bias statistics show sustained anti-LGBTQ hate incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented enforcement: county court found civil-rights violation for striking a trans woman (July 2026); hate-crime penalty enhancements since 2019; national hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Working civil-rights enforcement means assaults have a realistic remedy, unlike paper-only protections.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order challenges unresolved; facility-ban remedy undocumented; division arrest/flagged 'Do Not Travel' status unknown; incident rate per capita unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ and equality maps provide practical guidance; several federal orders blocked or enjoined; documented state enforcement success.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy quality varies by stage: services and assault have shown outcomes; border and federal facilities have not.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A there is a birth-sex facility exclusion for government buildings with no documented exemption or remedy, plus stronger entry-document scrutiny absent from that anchor. But unlike 0.35-A's courts routinely rejecting complaints, this division documents working civil-rights enforcement (2026 conviction-level finding), hate-crime enhancements and 88% public support, so it sits above that floor.

Closest match: a universal state-imposed exposure (federal facility exclusion and entry-document refusal) persisting with no shown remedy, alongside residents who are broadly supportive and courts that do convict attackers. 0.45-D's transport searches are narrower than this dossier's combination of border fraud risk plus custody conversion-therapy policy, pulling this slightly below it.

0.65-A has accepted borders, no facility ban and mostly functioning remedies with only uneven regional police. This case has documented tier-1 federal facility exclusion, entry-refusal instructions and state-perpetrated custody abuse — exposures 0.65-A entirely lacks — outweighing its comparable service protections and social tolerance, so it rates materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two systems. The federal layer supplies the heaviest exposures: entry adjudication told to refuse on sex discrepancy with fraud-based lifetime bar, exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities, and custody regimes documented harming trans detainees — none cancelled by state law. The division supplies the protections: enforced public-accommodations and employment rights, hate-crime enhancements, abolished panic defence, a state court protecting trans students, and 88% public support, with documented 2026 enforcement against an assault on a trans woman. Net: everyday service and street exposure is moderated and remediable, but every trans visitor carries continuous federal facility and document exposure, and detention escalates sharply in severity. For a traveller with a trans minor, the state's youth-care and sports bans add a distinct exposure.
